note: Budgets are a RATCHET against ACCIDENTAL bloat, not a hard product limit. Raise them
deliberately when a release adds real user-facing surface; never raise them to make a red
gate go away. check-bundle-size.mjs reads only `bundles[*].from/exports/maxRawBytes/
maxGzipBytes`, so this `note` key is inert (JSON carries no comments).

2.0.0 — MEASUREMENT FIX FIRST, THEN A DELIBERATE RAISE. Two separate things, in order:
(1) check-bundle-size.mjs now builds with `splitting: true` and reports the EAGER set — the
entry chunk plus everything reachable from it through import STATEMENTS, walked off esbuild's
metafile. Before, `bundle: true` with splitting off gave esbuild nowhere to put a dynamic
import, so it inlined it. 2.0 loads `mcp/resolve` through `await import()` only when a call
passes `options.mcp`, and the old pipeline billed all 15.5 KB of it to everyone who imports
the package. tsup.config.ts already sets `splitting: true`, and every real consumer bundler
code-splits a dynamic import, so the new number is the one that matches the shipped artifact.
Lazy chunks are still weighed under `maxLazyRawBytes`/`maxLazyGzipBytes` — nothing ships
unmeasured; the lazy weight just gets its own ratchet instead of inflating the cost of an import.
(2) With the measurement honest, core/edge were STILL over — that part is real eager growth,
and all of it sits in the agentic loop, reachable from streamChat/generateText:
- guardrails: the three evaluators in inference/loop-shared.ts plus the input/tool-call/output
call sites in both loops (src/guardrails.ts itself is a separate subpath and tree-shakes out)
- handoff interception: the transfer partition, the active-agent overlay and the wire rebuild
- context-overflow auto-recovery: recoverFromOverflow + the once-per-step retry gate in both loops
- memory/compaction wiring: scorer + maxChars + expandLinks threading, writePolicy gating,
memory observe events, the rolling-summary fold prompt, and recall-overhead token accounting
- the MCP hot-swap block (the resolver behind it is the lazy chunk; only the seam is eager)

2.0.0 — THE NEW SUBPATHS GET BUDGETS BEFORE THEY SHIP. Sprint 3 is the precedent: ~10 KB of
new surface went out unmeasured because nothing listed it here, and an unlisted subpath is
invisible to this ratchet. Measured through the same pipeline, ~10% headroom each:
transcription  20222 B raw / 7149 B gzip  ->  limits 22250 / 7870   (+10.0% / +10.1%)
guardrails       813 B raw /  493 B gzip  ->  limits   900 /  550   (+10.7% / +11.6%)
`guardrails` is two closures over type-only imports, and that near-zero number is the point:
it is the assertion that a built-in guardrail stays a value, not a subsystem.
NOT BUDGETED, and it is not an oversight: `./mcp/node`, `./stores/sqlite`, `./stores/redis`
and `./stores/postgres`. This checker builds with `platform: 'browser'` and the browser export
condition, so a Node-only subpath does not merely measure large — esbuild cannot resolve it at
all and the whole run THROWS (`Could not resolve "fs/promises"` / `"http"` for ./mcp/node).
Adding one here takes the gate red for every bundle, including the ones it was protecting.
Their edge-safety guard is `tooling/check-runtime-compat.mjs` instead, whose node-only input
regex names all four: it fails if a browser/edge consumer can so much as REACH them.
The same holds for the 2.3 Redis stores `./ops/redis` and `./swarm/redis` (lazy `redis` peer),
which the runtime check lists as Node-only entries and negative controls.
`./headless` (2.3 preview) is Node-only too (lazy node:fs/promises, node:path, node:process) and is
listed there as a Node-only entry, not budgeted here.
core/edge/lazy are untouched by the 2.0 publication surface. The new barrel exports (handoff,
the built-in guardrails, compactMessages on the root; handoff + guardrails on edge) tree-shake
out of the measured export sets — verified by bundling the previous barrels side by side with
the new ones: core came back byte-identical.
2.1.0 — OPTIONAL FEATURE ISOLATION, WITHOUT RAISING THE EAGER OR MCP LIMITS.
Native request admission, legacy optional usage pricing, and optional memory recall/extraction
load through narrow dynamic entries only when enabled. Native model/tool policy checks keep
the same implementation and fatal errors. Memory keeps its existing best-effort promises.
Source pipeline measurements: core eager 150490/46930, edge 138501/42946 raw/gzip bytes.
The optional roots measured native-request 2283/1077, usage-cost 1330/606 and memory-pipeline
10279/4309. Independent limits below carry approximately 10-13% headroom. The checker follows
each root's static dependency closure, excludes already-eager chunks, and counts shared lazy
dependencies against every owning feature. Unclassified lazy chunks fail. MCP retains its
existing 18500/7050 limit and can never borrow a new feature's allowance.
Native public surfaces also have explicit eager budgets: native-agent measured 175024/54470
and native-swarm 176912/55810 through the export sets below, with approximately 10% headroom.
Their native-request lazy roots are smaller (1396/745 and 1401/747) because policy definitions
are already eagerly required by these opt-in APIs; their own lazy cap is correspondingly lower.
